cka-exam-tips-2025.titleEn: CKA 2025: what I would have liked to know before taking the exam
cka-exam-tips-2025.excerptEn: I passed the CKA in March 2025 with a score of 91%. Here are my real prep notes: traps, speed tricks, and areas where people waste time.
cka-exam-tips-2025.contentEn:
Final score: **91%**. Remaining time: 8 minutes out of 120. Here's what I wish I knew.

## Exam Format (2025)

- **17 practical tasks ** in a real terminal environment
- **120 minutes** (yes, it's short)
- ** Minimum score **: 66%
- ** Authorized documentation **: kubernetes.io/docs only
- ** Domain weights **:

| Area | Weight |
|---|---|
| Storage | 10% |
| Troubleshooting | 30% |
| Workloads & Scheduling | 15% |
| Architecture Cluster | 25% |
| Services & Networking | 20% |

## Preparing your work environment

First thing to do at the beginning of the exam:

```bash
# Alias
alias k=kubectl
export do="--dry-run=client -o yaml"
export now="--grace-period=0 --force"

# Auto-completion
source <(kubectl completion bash)
complete -F __start_kubectl k
```

These 4 lines will save you 15-20 minutes on the exam.

## Mandatory orders (do not generate YAML by hand)

```bash
# Pod
k run nginx --image=nginx $do > pod.yaml

# Deployment
k create deployment app --image=nginx --replicas=3$do > deploy.yaml

# Service (exposes a deployment)
k expose deployment app --port=80 --target-port=8080 --type=ClusterIP $do > svc.yaml

# ConfigMap
k create configmap myconfig --from-literal=key=value $do

# Secret
k create secret generic mysecret --from-literal=password=s3cr3t $do

# ServiceAccount
k create serviceaccount mysa -n mynamespace $do

# Role + RoleBinding in one order
k create role pod-reader --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods $do
k create rolebinding pod-reader-binding --role=pod-reader --user=alice $do
```

## Domain 1: Troubleshooting (30%   most important)

This is where the exam is won or lost. Typical scenarios:

## # Pod not starting

```bash
k describe pod <name>    # Regarder Events
k logs <pod>             # Logs du conteneur
k logs <pod> --previous  # Logs avant le dernier crash
```

### Node NotReady

```bash
k describe node <name>   # Conditions, events
ssh <node>               # Si accès possible
systemctl status kubelet
journalctl -u kubelet -n 50
```

### Problème réseau

```bash
# Vérifier que les endpoints existent
k get endpoints <service>

# Test DNS resolution
k run test --rm -it --image=busybox -- nslookup<service>.<namespace>

# Check NetworkPolicies
k get networkpolicies -A
```

## Domain 2: Architecture Cluster (25%)

What often falls:

### ETCD backup & restore

```bash
# Backup
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /opt/backup/etcd.db \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key

# Verify
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /opt/backup/etcd.db

# Restore (remember flags!)
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore /opt/backup/etcd.db \
  --data-dir=/var/lib/etcd-restore
```

### Cluster Upgrade

```bash
# On the control plane
kubeadm upgrade plan
kubeadm upgrade apply v1.29.0

# Upgrade kubelet
apt-get update && apt-get install -y kubelet=1.29.0-1.1
systemctl restart kubelet

# On worker nodes
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
# ... upgrade on node ...
kubectl uncordon <node>
```

## Domain 3: Storage (10%)

```bash
# PersistentVolume
k get pv,pvc -A

# Example of PVC
k create -f - << EoF
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: my-pvc
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  storageClassName: standard

EoF ```

## Classic traps

1. **Forget `-n<namespace>`**: 30% of tasks specify a non-default namespace.
2. **Read the whole question **: often there is a kubectl context to change with `kubectl config use-context`.
3. **Waste time on a hard task **: If a task is worth 4% and takes 20 minutes, move on to the next one.
4. **Do not check his work**: after each task, do a `kubectl get` to confirm.

## Revision schedule (4 weeks)

| Week | Focus |
|---|---|
| S1 | Killer.sh mock exam 1   identify gaps |
| S2 | Review weak areas + practical labs |
| S3 | Killer.sh mock exam 2 + timing |
| S4 | Slight revision, rest 2d before the exam |

> **Killer.sh** (included in the certification) is more difficult than the real exam. If you can do it, you're ready.
